decisions.rationale: Full name of a single defined syndrome, linked to one specific definition with no further categorization. The whole phrase is kept as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: The disease name is used adjectivally to modify the noun 'features' (phenotypic features of the patient), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: Duplicate mention of the same specific syndrome name in the title; duplicates are annotated separately.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions); What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: Abbreviation of Borjeson-Forssman-Lehmann syndrome, which is a synonymous mention of the same specific disease and is annotated as a separate mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions); What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'Syndromal X-linked mental retardation' refers to a family of multiple specific syndromes rather than one defined disease, matching the guideline example of 'X-linked mental retardation syndrome' as a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class); Examples 12 (Disease Class)

decisions.rationale: 'BFLS-like' describes the patient as resembling BFLS and modifies the noun 'patient', so it functions as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: 'BFLS syndrome' names the same single specific disease (Borjeson-Forssman-Lehmann syndrome) in the abstract, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions)

decisions.rationale: The contiguous string coordinates two distinct disease mentions, 'syndromal forms' and 'non-specific forms' of X-linked mental retardation, sharing a head noun; splitting it would lose information, so it is one Composite Mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 (Composite Mention for contiguous strings with multiple disease mentions); Examples 7 (Composite Mention)
